claim: The new cryo-EM structure of Vps4 bound to an ESCRT-III peptide substrate has a resolution of 3.2 Å.
source: Building upon our earlier 4.3 Å resolution cryo-EM structure (Monroe et al., 2017), we now report a 3.2 Å structure of Vps4 bound to an ESCRT-III peptide substrate.
evidence: The resolution is stated directly in the abstract and confirmed in the methods section with FSC curves and reconstruction statistics.

claim: The ESCRT-III peptide approximates a β-strand conformation in the Vps4 structure.
source: The new structure reveals that the peptide approximates a β-strand conformation whose helical symmetry matches that of the five Vps4 subunits it contacts directly.
evidence: The peptide conformation is described with specific phi and psi angles (phi −92° to −151°; psi 102° to 189° (−171°)) that are characteristic of β-strands.

claim: Adjacent Vps4 subunits make equivalent interactions with successive substrate dipeptides through two distinct classes of side chain binding pockets.
source: Adjacent Vps4 subunits make equivalent interactions with successive substrate dipeptides through two distinct classes of side chain binding pockets formed primarily by Vps4 pore loop 1.
evidence: The structure shows class I and class II pockets with specific residue interactions documented in Figure 3.

claim: The side chain binding pockets are formed primarily by Vps4 pore loop 1.
source: Adjacent Vps4 subunits make equivalent interactions with successive substrate dipeptides through two distinct classes of side chain binding pockets formed primarily by Vps4 pore loop 1.
evidence: The structural data shows that K205, W206, and M207 from pore loop 1 form the binding pockets.

claim: The structure supports a 'conveyor belt' model of translocation.
source: The structure supports a 'conveyor belt' model of translocation in which ATP binding allows a Vps4 subunit to join the growing end of the helix and engage the substrate, while hydrolysis and release promotes helix disassembly and substrate release at the lagging end.
evidence: The mechanistic model is inferred from the structural arrangement of subunits and their interactions with substrate and nucleotides.

claim: ATP binding allows a Vps4 subunit to join the growing end of the helix and engage the substrate.
source: The structure supports a 'conveyor belt' model of translocation in which ATP binding allows a Vps4 subunit to join the growing end of the helix and engage the substrate, while hydrolysis and release promotes helix disassembly and substrate release at the lagging end.
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation based on the structural states observed and nucleotide binding patterns.

claim: ATP hydrolysis and release promotes helix disassembly and substrate release at the lagging end.
source: The structure supports a 'conveyor belt' model of translocation in which ATP binding allows a Vps4 subunit to join the growing end of the helix and engage the substrate, while hydrolysis and release promotes helix disassembly and substrate release at the lagging end.
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation based on the structural states observed and nucleotide binding patterns.

claim: The ESCRT pathway drives multiple cellular membrane fission processes.
source: The Endosomal Sorting Complexes Required for Transport (ESCRT) pathway drives multiple cellular membrane fission processes (Christ et al., 2017; Scourfield and Martin-Serrano, 2017) through the formation of filaments comprising different subsets of related ESCRT-III family members.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: ESCRT-III filaments stabilize highly curved membrane necks that resolve by fission when the filaments are remodeled by Vps4.
source: ESCRT-III filaments stabilize highly curved membrane necks that resolve by fission when the filaments are remodeled by Vps4 (Monroe and Hill, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Continued Vps4 activity removes ESCRT-III subunits and drives complete filament disassembly.
source: Continued Vps4 activity removes ESCRT-III subunits and drives complete filament disassembly, thereby enabling subsequent rounds of ESCRT activity (Mierzwa et al., 2017; Schöneberg et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Vps4 is monomeric or dimeric at cytoplasmic concentrations.
source: Vps4 is monomeric or dimeric at cytoplasmic concentrations, but forms a hexamer when active and recruited to ESCRT-III filaments (Monroe et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Vps4 forms a hexamer when active and recruited to ESCRT-III filaments.
source: Vps4 is monomeric or dimeric at cytoplasmic concentrations, but forms a hexamer when active and recruited to ESCRT-III filaments (Monroe et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Recruitment of Vps4 is mediated by binding of the Vps4 MIT domains to MIM elements in the exposed tails of ESCRT-III subunits.
source: Recruitment is mediated, at least in part, by binding of the Vps4 MIT (Microtubule Interacting and Transport) domains to MIM (MIT Interacting Motif) elements in the exposed tails of ESCRT-III subunits (Obita et al., 2007; Stuchell-Brereton et al., 2007; Hurley and Yang, 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Hexamerization of Vps4 is promoted by the cofactor protein Vta1/LIP5.
source: Hexamerization is further promoted by the cofactor protein Vta1/LIP5 (Scott et al., 2005; Lottridge et al., 2006; Azmi et al., 2008; Xiao et al., 2008), whose VSL domain binds adjacent Vps4 subunits at the ring periphery (Yang and Hurley, 2010; Davies et al., 2014; Monroe et al., 2017; Sun et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The VSL domain of Vta1/LIP5 binds adjacent Vps4 subunits at the ring periphery.
source: Hexamerization is further promoted by the cofactor protein Vta1/LIP5 (Scott et al., 2005; Lottridge et al., 2006; Azmi et al., 2008; Xiao et al., 2008), whose VSL domain binds adjacent Vps4 subunits at the ring periphery (Yang and Hurley, 2010; Davies et al., 2014; Monroe et al., 2017; Sun et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The Vps4 N-terminal MIT domain is followed by an ~40 residue flexible linker and an ATPase cassette.
source: The Vps4 N-terminal MIT domain is followed by an ~40 residue flexible linker and an ATPase cassette that comprises a large ATPase domain, small ATPase domain, and a β domain (Scott et al., 2005).
evidence: This structural organization is described with a citation to previous work.

claim: The Vps4 ATPase cassette comprises a large ATPase domain, small ATPase domain, and a β domain.
source: The Vps4 N-terminal MIT domain is followed by an ~40 residue flexible linker and an ATPase cassette that comprises a large ATPase domain, small ATPase domain, and a β domain (Scott et al., 2005).
evidence: This structural organization is described with a citation to previous work.

claim: Recently reported cryo-EM structures of Vps4 at overall resolutions of 4.3 Å, 6.1 Å, and 3.9 Å revealed similar hexameric 'lock washers'.
source: Recently reported cryo-EM structures of Vps4 at overall resolutions of 4.3 Å (Monroe et al., 2017), 6.1 Å (Su et al., 2017), and 3.9 Å (Sun et al., 2017) revealed similar hexameric 'lock washers', in which five of the six Vps4 subunits form a helical assembly and the sixth closes the ring.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous cryo-EM structures.

claim: In the hexameric 'lock washer' structure, five of the six Vps4 subunits form a helical assembly and the sixth closes the ring.
source: Recently reported cryo-EM structures of Vps4 at overall resolutions of 4.3 Å (Monroe et al., 2017), 6.1 Å (Su et al., 2017), and 3.9 Å (Sun et al., 2017) revealed similar hexameric 'lock washers', in which five of the six Vps4 subunits form a helical assembly and the sixth closes the ring.
evidence: This structural arrangement is described with citations to previous cryo-EM structures.

claim: The hexameric arrangement in cryo-EM structures is quite different from the packing seen in multiple Vps4 crystal structures.
source: This arrangement is quite different from the packing seen in multiple Vps4 crystal structures.
evidence: This is a comparative observation based on structural data.

claim: The earlier 4.3 Å structure guided the proposal that ESCRT-III substrates bind within the hexamer pore.
source: Our structure, which was visualized in complex with a substrate peptide, guided the proposal that ESCRT-III substrates bind within the hexamer pore (Monroe et al., 2017), consistent with a model that ESCRT-III subunits are unfolded by translocation through the pore (Yang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a reference to a previous mechanistic proposal based on structural data.

claim: The substrate binding model is consistent with ESCRT-III subunits being unfolded by translocation through the pore.
source: Our structure, which was visualized in complex with a substrate peptide, guided the proposal that ESCRT-III substrates bind within the hexamer pore (Monroe et al., 2017), consistent with a model that ESCRT-III subunits are unfolded by translocation through the pore (Yang et al., 2015).
evidence: This mechanistic model is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: An alternative proposal suggested that substrates are engaged by a single ESCRT-III subunit and ATP hydrolysis pulls an entire ESCRT-III subunit from the filament.
source: In contrast, the observation that the Vps4 hexamer adopts 'open' and 'closed' states in the absence of Vta1/LIP5 and substrate, prompted the proposal that substrates are engaged by a single ESCRT-III subunit, and that ATP hydrolysis pulls an entire ESCRT-III subunit from the filament and positions the next Vps4 subunit to remove the ensuing ESCRT-III subunit (Su et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a reference to an alternative mechanistic model proposed by others.

claim: The six Vps4 subunits form a closed ring with six Vta1 VSL domains binding around the periphery and a single ESCRT-III peptide bound in the central pore.
source: The six Vps4 subunits form a closed ring, with six Vta1 VSL domains binding around the periphery and a single ESCRT-III peptide bound in the central pore (Figure 1, Table 1, Figure 1—figure supplements 1–4, Figure 1—video 1).
evidence: This structural arrangement is directly observed in the cryo-EM reconstruction.

claim: Vps4 subunits A-E form a helix whose symmetry approximates a 60° rotation and 6.3 Å translation between adjacent subunits.
source: Vps4 subunits A-E form a helix whose symmetry approximates a 60° rotation and 6.3 Å translation between adjacent subunits, and provides the binding surface for the ESCRT-III peptide.
evidence: The helical parameters are measured from the structural data.

claim: Subunit E deviates slightly from the more exact helical symmetry of subunits A-D.
source: As noted previously (Monroe et al., 2017), subunit E deviates slightly from the more exact helical symmetry of subunits A-D.
evidence: This structural observation is noted with reference to previous work.

claim: The large domain of subunit F is disengaged from adjacent Vps4 subunits and substrate and appears to be transitioning between the two ends of the Vps4 helix.
source: The large domain of subunit F is disengaged from adjacent Vps4 subunits (and substrate) and appears to be transitioning between the two ends of the Vps4 helix.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the structural state of subunit F based on its position and contacts.

claim: Subunit F and features at the ring periphery, including the Vps4 β domains and the Vta1 VSL domains, have weak density.
source: Subunit F and features at the ring periphery, including the Vps4 β domains and the Vta1 VSL domains, have weak density.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the cryo-EM density map.

claim: Nucleotides primarily contact one Vps4 subunit at a subunit interface, with the β-phosphate and BeFx contacting two 'finger' arginines, R288 and R289, from the following subunit.
source: Nucleotides primarily contact one Vps4 subunit at a subunit interface, with the β-phosphate and BeFx contacting two 'finger' arginines, R288 and R289, from the following subunit (Figure 2, Figure 2—videos 1–5).
evidence: The nucleotide coordination is directly observed in the structure.

claim: The bound ADP·BeFx mimics ATP binding to subunits A, B, and C.
source: The bound ADP·BeFx mimics ATP binding to subunits A, B, and C, whereas subunits D and E appear to bind ADP.
evidence: The nucleotide states are interpreted from the density and coordination patterns.

claim: Subunits D and E appear to bind ADP.
source: The bound ADP·BeFx mimics ATP binding to subunits A, B, and C, whereas subunits D and E appear to bind ADP.
evidence: The nucleotide states are interpreted from the density and coordination patterns.

claim: The density of subunit F is too weak to reliably assess the presence of nucleotide, and it may be empty.
source: The density of subunit F is too weak to reliably assess the presence of nucleotide, and it may be empty.
evidence: This is an assessment of the density quality and interpretation.

claim: The coordination of bound nucleotides is similar for all Vps4 subunits and resembles binding to other ATPases.
source: The coordination of bound nucleotides is similar for all Vps4 subunits, and resembles binding to other ATPases (Wendler et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a comparative observation with citation to other ATPase structures.

claim: The hinge angle between large and small domains does not change substantially with the bound nucleotide.
source: In contrast to earlier proposals (Gonciarz et al., 2008), the hinge angle between large and small domains does not change substantially with the bound nucleotide, being 120–121° for subunits A-D, 117° for subunit E, and 122° for subunit F.
evidence: The hinge angles are measured from the structural data and contradict a previous proposal.

claim: The AB, BC, and CD interfaces are extensive, similar to each other, and include large domain contacts with adjacent large domains and small domains.
source: The AB, BC, and CD interfaces are extensive, similar to each other, and include large domain contacts with adjacent large domains and small domains (Figure 2—videos 6,7).
evidence: The interface characteristics are observed in the structure.

claim: Comparison of the AB, BC, CD interfaces with the DE subunit pair shows an ~8° rotation of subunit E which maintains very similar contacts with the preceding D subunit.
source: Comparison of these interfaces with the DE subunit pair shows an ~8° rotation of subunit E which, nevertheless, maintains very similar contacts with the preceding D subunit and relative positions of pore loops (Figure 2—video 8).
evidence: The rotation and contacts are measured from the structural data.

claim: It is uncertain why the AB, BC, and CD interfaces bind ATP (ADP·BeFx) while the similar DE interface appears to bind ADP.
source: It is therefore uncertain why the AB, BC, and CD interfaces bind ATP (ADP·BeFx) while the similar DE interface appears to bind ADP.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of uncertainty in interpreting the nucleotide states.

claim: The finding that subunit E binds ADP at the interface with subunit F supports the mechanistic model that ATP hydrolysis at subunit D destabilizes the subunit interface.
source: Regardless, the finding that subunit E binds ADP at the interface with subunit F further supports our mechanistic model that ATP hydrolysis at subunit D destabilizes the subunit interface to promote formation of the more open nucleotide binding site seen for subunit E (below).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the structural data in support of a mechanistic model.

claim: Contacts involving the small ATPase domains remain more similar across subunit interfaces compared to large domain contacts.
source: In contrast to the major disruption in contacts between the large domain of subunit F and the large domains of its neighbors, contacts involving the small ATPase domains remain more similar.
evidence: This is a comparative observation of interface contacts in the structure.

claim: The F small domain to A large domain contacts are closely superimposable with those of AB, BC, CD, and DE.
source: This is especially true for the FA interface, where the F small domain to A large domain contacts are closely superimposable with those of AB, BC, CD, and DE (Figure 2—video 9).
evidence: This is observed through structural superposition.

claim: The E small domain to F large domain contacts are mediated by the same hydrophobic contacts, albeit with a rotation of ~25° and attendant shifts of 4.5–7.5 Å.
source: The E small domain to F large domain contacts are mediated by the same hydrophobic contacts, albeit with a rotation of ~25° and attendant shifts of 4.5–7.5 Å.
evidence: The rotation and shifts are measured from the structural data.

claim: The small domain-large domain interaction appears to be maintained throughout the reaction cycle as subunits transition from the lagging to the leading end of the Vps4 helix.
source: Thus, this interaction appears to be maintained throughout the reaction cycle as subunits transition from the lagging (subunit E) to the leading (subunit A) end of the Vps4 helix, and may help maintain the hexameric assembly while the hydrolysis and release of ATP disrupts the core large domain contacts that define the ESCRT-III substrate-binding site.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the structural observations regarding the reaction cycle.

claim: The small domain-large domain interface may help maintain the hexameric assembly while ATP hydrolysis and release disrupts the core large domain contacts.
source: Thus, this interaction appears to be maintained throughout the reaction cycle as subunits transition from the lagging (subunit E) to the leading (subunit A) end of the Vps4 helix, and may help maintain the hexameric assembly while the hydrolysis and release of ATP disrupts the core large domain contacts that define the ESCRT-III substrate-binding site.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the functional role of the interface.

claim: The small domain-large domain interface is the major lattice contact in all of the reported crystal structures of Vps4.
source: Interestingly, the small domain-large domain interface is the major lattice contact in all of the reported crystal structures of Vps4, which totals 22 crystallographically unique contacts (Figure 2—video 10).
evidence: This is a comparative analysis of crystal structures.

claim: The archaeal Vps4 crystal contacts closely resemble the FA/AB/BC/CD/DE interface.
source: The archaeal Vps4 crystal contacts (Monroe et al., 2014; Caillat et al., 2015) closely resemble the FA/AB/BC/CD/DE interface, while eukaryotic crystal contacts (Scott et al., 2005; Xiao et al., 2007; Gonciarz et al., 2008; Inoue et al., 2008) overlap with the EF interface, except two of the three mouse Vps4 crystal contacts (Inoue et al., 2008), which are intermediate between the two states.
evidence: This is a comparative analysis of crystal structures with citations.

claim: Eukaryotic Vps4 crystal contacts overlap with the EF interface, except two of the three mouse Vps4 crystal contacts which are intermediate between the two states.
source: The archaeal Vps4 crystal contacts (Monroe et al., 2014; Caillat et al., 2015) closely resemble the FA/AB/BC/CD/DE interface, while eukaryotic crystal contacts (Scott et al., 2005; Xiao et al., 2007; Gonciarz et al., 2008; Inoue et al., 2008) overlap with the EF interface, except two of the three mouse Vps4 crystal contacts (Inoue et al., 2008), which are intermediate between the two states.
evidence: This is a comparative analysis of crystal structures with citations.

claim: The differences in crystal contacts correlate with the presence of a Vps4 β domain and Vta1 cofactor in eukaryotes but not archaea.
source: These differences correlate with the presence of a Vps4 β domain and Vta1 cofactor in eukaryotes but not archaea, supporting the interpretation that Vta1 promotes formation and maintenance of the closed helical substrate-binding assembly of Vps4.
evidence: This is a correlation observed between structural features and phylogenetic distribution.

claim: Vta1 promotes formation and maintenance of the closed helical substrate-binding assembly of Vps4.
source: These differences correlate with the presence of a Vps4 β domain and Vta1 cofactor in eukaryotes but not archaea, supporting the interpretation that Vta1 promotes formation and maintenance of the closed helical substrate-binding assembly of Vps4.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on structural and phylogenetic correlations.

claim: The DEIVNKVL ESCRT-III peptide is clearly defined in the new 3.2 Å map, with the exception of the first two side chains, D1 and E2.
source: The DEIVNKVL ESCRT-III peptide is clearly defined in the new 3.2 Å map (Figure 3—video 1), with the exception of the first two side chains, D1 and E2 (Vps2 D165 and E166), which have weak density, as is typically seen for carboxylates in cryo-EM maps (Mitsuoka et al., 1999; Bartesaghi et al., 2014; Yonekura et al., 2015; Hryc et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the cryo-EM density map with citations explaining the weak density for carboxylates.

claim: The first two side chains of the ESCRT-III peptide, D1 and E2, have weak density, as is typically seen for carboxylates in cryo-EM maps.
source: The DEIVNKVL ESCRT-III peptide is clearly defined in the new 3.2 Å map (Figure 3—video 1), with the exception of the first two side chains, D1 and E2 (Vps2 D165 and E166), which have weak density, as is typically seen for carboxylates in cryo-EM maps (Mitsuoka et al., 1999; Bartesaghi et al., 2014; Yonekura et al., 2015; Hryc et al., 2017).
evidence: This observation is explained with citations to literature on cryo-EM density characteristics.

claim: The assigned peptide orientation was validated by building and refining in the reverse direction, which showed a correlation coefficient of 0.85 for the assigned orientation vs. 0.81 in the reversed orientation.
source: The assigned peptide orientation was validated by building and refining in the reverse direction, which showed a correlation coefficient of 0.85 for the assigned orientation vs. 0.81 in the reversed orientation, and EMRinger (Barad et al., 2015) scores of 3.7 for the assigned orientation vs. 1.1 for the reversed orientation (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This validation was performed using quantitative metrics comparing the two orientations.

claim: EMRinger scores were 3.7 for the assigned peptide orientation vs. 1.1 for the reversed orientation.
source: The assigned peptide orientation was validated by building and refining in the reverse direction, which showed a correlation coefficient of 0.85 for the assigned orientation vs. 0.81 in the reversed orientation, and EMRinger (Barad et al., 2015) scores of 3.7 for the assigned orientation vs. 1.1 for the reversed orientation (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This validation was performed using the EMRinger metric.

claim: The peptide adopts an extended conformation with phi angles of −92° to −151° and psi angles of 102° to 189° (−171°).
source: The peptide adopts an extended conformation that resembles a canonical β-strand (phi −92° to −151°; psi 102° to 189° (−171°)) and packs closely against Vps4 subunits A-E (Figure 3, Figure 3—videos 2–4).
evidence: The dihedral angles are measured from the refined structure.

claim: Odd-numbered ESCRT-III residues (D1, I3, N5, V7) bind in 'class I' pockets.
source: Odd-numbered ESCRT-III residues (D1, I3, N5, V7) bind in 'class I' pockets, while the side chains of even-numbered ESCRT-III residues (E2, V4, K6, L8) bind in 'class II' pockets.
evidence: This binding pattern is observed in the structure.

claim: Even-numbered ESCRT-III residues (E2, V4, K6, L8) bind in 'class II' pockets.
source: Odd-numbered ESCRT-III residues (D1, I3, N5, V7) bind in 'class I' pockets, while the side chains of even-numbered ESCRT-III residues (E2, V4, K6, L8) bind in 'class II' pockets.
evidence: This binding pattern is observed in the structure.

claim: Class I pockets are formed by pore loop 1 residues K205 and W206, with substrate side chains sandwiched between W206 from successive subunits.
source: Class I pockets are formed by pore loop 1 residues K205 and W206, with substrate side chains sandwiched between W206 from successive subunits.
evidence: The pocket composition is observed in the structure.

claim: The class I pocket is flanked by K205 from the first Vps4 subunit, which may also stabilize the ladder of W206 side chains through cation-π interactions.
source: The pocket is flanked by K205 from the first Vps4 subunit, which may also stabilize the ladder of W206 side chains through cation-π interactions.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the structural arrangement.

claim: Class II pockets are formed by the pore loop 1 M207 residues of successive subunits.
source: The class II pockets are formed by the pore loop 1 M207 residues of successive subunits, and are flanked by pore loop 2 residues of the first Vps4 subunit and, to a greater extent, by the pore loop 2 residues of the preceding subunit.
evidence: The pocket composition is observed in the structure.

claim: Class II pockets are flanked by pore loop 2 residues of the first Vps4 subunit and, to a greater extent, by the pore loop 2 residues of the preceding subunit.
source: The class II pockets are formed by the pore loop 1 M207 residues of successive subunits, and are flanked by pore loop 2 residues of the first Vps4 subunit and, to a greater extent, by the pore loop 2 residues of the preceding subunit.
evidence: The pocket composition is observed in the structure.

claim: The first class II pocket is incompletely formed because the pore loop 2 residues of the preceding subunit (F) are not yet in position.
source: The first of these pockets, which includes M207 residues of the A and B subunits, is incompletely formed because the pore loop 2 residues of the preceding subunit (F) are not yet in position.
evidence: This is an observation of the structural state of the first pocket.

claim: The three pore loop 2 residues that most closely approach the peptide (E245, S246, E247) do not make distinctive contacts with the ESCRT-III peptide.
source: The three pore loop 2 residues that most closely approach the peptide (E245, S246, E247) do not make distinctive contacts with the ESCRT-III peptide.
evidence: This is an observation of the lack of specific interactions in the structure.

claim: S246 caps the N-terminus of a Vps4 helix.
source: S246 caps the N-terminus of a Vps4 helix while E245 and E247 make non-specific contacts with peptide side chains.
evidence: This is a structural observation.

claim: E245 and E247 make non-specific contacts with peptide side chains.
source: S246 caps the N-terminus of a Vps4 helix while E245 and E247 make non-specific contacts with peptide side chains.
evidence: This is a structural observation.

claim: The different class I and class II pockets are all essentially identical.
source: The different class I and class II pockets are all essentially identical (Figure 3CD) and their exposure to the highly solvated pore explains how polar side chains can be accommodated.
evidence: This is observed through structural superposition of the pockets.

claim: The exposure of the pockets to the highly solvated pore explains how polar side chains can be accommodated.
source: The different class I and class II pockets are all essentially identical (Figure 3CD) and their exposure to the highly solvated pore explains how polar side chains can be accommodated.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the structural features explaining substrate accommodation.

claim: The NH groups of the even-numbered ESCRT-III peptide residues form hydrogen bonds with the main chain O of Vps4 K205.
source: The refined model indicates that the NH groups of the even-numbered ESCRT-III peptide residues form hydrogen bonds with the main chain O of Vps4 K205 (subunit A, B, C, and D distances are 3.1–3.5 Å).
evidence: The hydrogen bonds are identified in the refined model with specific distances.

claim: The distances between NH groups of even-numbered ESCRT-III residues and main chain O of Vps4 K205 are 3.1–3.5 Å for subunits A, B, C, and D.
source: The refined model indicates that the NH groups of the even-numbered ESCRT-III peptide residues form hydrogen bonds with the main chain O of Vps4 K205 (subunit A, B, C, and D distances are 3.1–3.5 Å).
evidence: These distances are measured from the refined model.

claim: In the reverse peptide orientation, the distances between NH groups and K205 O are 3.4–4.5 Å.
source: In contrast, these distances are 3.4–4.5 Å in the model refined with the peptide in the reverse orientation.
evidence: These distances are measured from the model refined in the reverse orientation.

claim: Substrate NH hydrogen bonds may help define the substrate orientation by optimally positioning ESCRT-III side chains with respect to their binding pockets.
source: Thus, substrate NH hydrogen bonds may help define the substrate orientation by optimally positioning ESCRT-III side chains with respect to their binding pockets (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the functional role of the hydrogen bonds.

claim: The enzyme proceeds by transitioning of subunit configurations around the hexameric ring, such that one step represents transitioning of subunits F, A, B, C, D, E to the configurations of subunits A, B, C, D, E, F.
source: We envision that the enzyme proceeds by transitioning of subunit configurations around the hexameric ring, such that one step represents transitioning of subunits F, A, B, C, D, E to the configurations of subunits A, B, C, D, E, F (Figure 4A, Figure 4—video 1).
evidence: This is a mechanistic model proposed based on the structural observations.

claim: Each step comprises concomitant changes in subunit interfaces at each end of the Vps4 A-E helix.
source: Each step comprises concomitant changes in subunit interfaces at each end of the Vps4 A-E helix.
evidence: This is part of the mechanistic model based on structural observations.

claim: At the leading end, binding of ATP allows subunit F to pack against subunit A and thereby bind the next two residues of the substrate.
source: At the leading end, binding of ATP allows subunit F to pack against subunit A and thereby bind the next two residues of the substrate.
evidence: This is part of the mechanistic model based on structural observations.

claim: At the lagging end, hydrolysis of ATP and subsequent phosphate release destabilizes the interface and drives subunit E to the transitioning configuration.
source: At the lagging end, hydrolysis of ATP and subsequent phosphate release destabilizes the interface and drives subunit E to the transitioning configuration, thereby opening the nucleotide binding site to allow exchange of ADP by ATP.
evidence: This is part of the mechanistic model based on structural observations.

claim: The equivalent dipeptide-binding sites formed at the interfaces of subunits A-E track with their bound dipeptides along the pore as subunits transition from the lagging end to the leading end of the helix.
source: In this manner, the equivalent dipeptide-binding sites formed at the interfaces of subunits A-E track with their bound dipeptides along the pore as subunits transition from the lagging end to the leading end of the helix.
evidence: This is part of the mechanistic model based on structural observations.

claim: The pathway can be represented either as Vps4 'walking' along the substrate or as substrate being translocated through the Vps4 pore, depending upon the frame of reference.
source: Thus, the pathway can be represented either as Vps4 'walking' along the substrate or as substrate being translocated through the Vps4 pore, depending upon the frame of reference.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the mechanistic model from different perspectives.

claim: The model implies that each step translocates two amino acid residues and hydrolyses one ATP molecule.
source: Our model implies that each step translocates two amino acid residues and hydrolyses one ATP molecule.
evidence: This is a prediction from the mechanistic model.

claim: The model explains the importance of the pore loop residues and the integral role of the class I and II pockets.
source: It also explains the importance of the pore loop residues and the integral role of the class I and II pockets, because once a substrate residue binds at the top of the Vps4 helix it does not substantially change conformation until released at the bottom of the helical conveyor belt.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the functional significance of structural features.

claim: Once a substrate residue binds at the top of the Vps4 helix it does not substantially change conformation until released at the bottom of the helical conveyor belt.
source: It also explains the importance of the pore loop residues and the integral role of the class I and II pockets, because once a substrate residue binds at the top of the Vps4 helix it does not substantially change conformation until released at the bottom of the helical conveyor belt.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the structural observations.

claim: The model is consistent with reports that other AAA+ ATPases bind a maximum of three or four ATP molecules.
source: The model is also consistent with reports that other AAA+ ATPases bind a maximum of three or four ATP molecules (Hersch et al., 2005; Horwitz et al., 2007; Yakamavich et al., 2008; Smith et al., 2011).
evidence: This consistency is noted with citations to previous literature.

claim: The mechanistic model is analogous to mechanisms established for translocation of DNA by the E1 helicase and of RNA by the Rho translocase.
source: Moreover, despite important structural differences, our mechanistic model is analogous to mechanisms established for translocation of DNA by the E1 helicase (Enemark and Joshua-Tor, 2006) and of RNA by the Rho translocase (Thomsen and Berger, 2009; Thomsen et al., 2016).
evidence: This analogy is drawn with citations to mechanisms of other molecular motors.

claim: Vps4 is a member of the classic clade of AAA+ ATPases.
source: Vps4 is a member of the classic clade of AAA+ ATPases, which includes the original members of the AAA ATPase family (Iyer et al., 2004; Erzberger and Berger, 2006).
evidence: This classification is stated with citations to previous literature.

claim: Classic clade AAA+ ATPases are hexameric protein translocases whose conserved pore loops emanate from equivalent structural elements.
source: These proteins are hexameric protein translocases, whose conserved pore loops emanate from equivalent structural elements, although their N-terminal domains are variable and only Vps4 has a β domain.
evidence: This is a general characterization of the protein family.

claim: Only Vps4 has a β domain among classic clade AAA+ ATPases.
source: These proteins are hexameric protein translocases, whose conserved pore loops emanate from equivalent structural elements, although their N-terminal domains are variable and only Vps4 has a β domain.
evidence: This is a distinguishing feature of Vps4 within the family.

claim: Vps4 is a homohexamer that forms a single ring.
source: For example, Vps4 is a homohexamer that forms a single ring, whereas p97/CDC48/VAT and NSF comprise two AAA ATPase cassettes that each form a hexameric ring.
evidence: This is a structural characteristic of Vps4.

claim: p97/CDC48/VAT and NSF comprise two AAA ATPase cassettes that each form a hexameric ring.
source: For example, Vps4 is a homohexamer that forms a single ring, whereas p97/CDC48/VAT and NSF comprise two AAA ATPase cassettes that each form a hexameric ring.
evidence: This is a structural characteristic of these AAA+ ATPases.

claim: HSP104/ClpB form a double ATPase ring structure in which only one of the rings belongs to the classic clade.
source: Others, such as HSP104/ClpB, form a double ATPase ring structure in which only one of the rings belongs to the classic clade.
evidence: This is a structural characteristic of HSP104/ClpB.

claim: The eukaryotic proteasome ATPases form part of a much larger complex and comprise six different, albeit related, subunits.
source: Still others, such as the eukaryotic proteasome ATPases, form part of a much larger complex and comprise six different, albeit related, subunits.
evidence: This is a structural characteristic of proteasome ATPases.

claim: Sequence alignment of classic clade AAA+ ATPase family members shows that the first two of the three pore loop 1 residues that contact substrate (Vps4 K205, W206, M207) are conserved.
source: Sequence alignment of classic clade AAA+ ATPase family members for which structures have been reported shows that the first two of the three pore loop 1 residues that contact substrate (Vps4 K205, W206, M207) are conserved (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This conservation is observed through sequence alignment.

claim: W206 is always W, F, or Y in classic clade AAA+ ATPases, all of which could perform the role of sandwiching substrate side chains.
source: W206 is always W, F, or Y, all of which could perform the role of sandwiching substrate side chains.
evidence: This conservation pattern is observed in sequence alignments with functional interpretation.

claim: The K205 residue is usually K but sometimes M, which like K could flank the class I binding pocket.
source: The preceding K205 residue is usually K but sometimes M, which like K could flank the class I binding pocket.
evidence: This conservation pattern is observed in sequence alignments with functional interpretation.

claim: The M207 residue is more variable but usually I, L or V, with examples of M, A, F, K, R, and Y, all of which could provide hydrophobic sides to the class II binding pocket.
source: The more variable third residue, M207, is usually I, L or V, but there are examples of M (Vps4), A, F, K, R, and Y, all of which could provide hydrophobic sides to the class II binding pocket.
evidence: This variability is observed in sequence alignments with functional interpretation.

claim: The G208 residue is invariant, presumably because it adopts phi angles (~81 to 85°) that are only favored for glycine.
source: Interestingly, the following residue, G208, is invariant, presumably because it adopts phi angles (~81 to 85°) that are only favored for glycine, and helps define a conformation that can pack against pore loop 1 residues from neighboring subunits.
evidence: This conservation is observed with a structural explanation for the invariance.

claim: G208 helps define a conformation that can pack against pore loop 1 residues from neighboring subunits.
source: Interestingly, the following residue, G208, is invariant, presumably because it adopts phi angles (~81 to 85°) that are only favored for glycine, and helps define a conformation that can pack against pore loop 1 residues from neighboring subunits.
evidence: This is a functional interpretation of the structural role of G208.

claim: Pore loop 2 residues are less conserved and are typically disordered in other published structures.
source: Pore loop 2 residues are less conserved and are typically disordered in other published structures, which is consistent with the lack of distinctive roles in contacting substrate.
evidence: This observation is made from comparison with other structures.

claim: The lack of conservation and disorder of pore loop 2 residues is consistent with the lack of distinctive roles in contacting substrate.
source: Pore loop 2 residues are less conserved and are typically disordered in other published structures, which is consistent with the lack of distinctive roles in contacting substrate.
evidence: This is an interpretation connecting structural observations to functional roles.

claim: The Vps4 structure superimposes closely with the recently reported structures of VAT, HSP104, and ClpB, which were each determined with substrate bound in their central pores.
source: Our Vps4 structure superimposes closely with the recently reported structures of VAT (Ripstein et al., 2017), HSP104 (Gates et al., 2017), and ClpB (Deville et al., 2017), which were each determined with substrate bound in their central pores, albeit at relatively low resolutions.
evidence: This structural similarity is observed through superposition with citations to the compared structures.

claim: A 3.4 Å structure of the YME1 AAA ATPase in complex with a mixed polypeptide substrate presents a very similar structure and mechanism to that described for Vps4.
source: A very recently published 3.4 Å structure of the YME1 AAA ATPase in complex with a mixed polypeptide substrate (Puchades et al., 2017) also presents a very similar structure and mechanism to that described here, although coordinates are not yet available during final preparation of this manuscript.
evidence: This similarity is noted with a citation to the YME1 structure.

claim: Close superposition is seen between Vps4 and multiple other classic clade AAA+ ATPases that have been visualized in the absence of substrate.
source: Close superposition is also seen with multiple other classic clade AAA+ ATPases that have been visualized in the absence of substrate (Figure 4B, Figure 4—video 2).
evidence: This structural similarity is observed through superposition.

claim: p97 and CDC48 structures display rotational rather than helical symmetry, which is a notable exception to the close superposition with Vps4.
source: Notable exceptions include p97 and CDC48, whose structures display rotational rather than helical symmetry (Banerjee et al., 2016; Xia et al., 2016), and ClpX and HslU, which are not members of the classic clade but share notable similarities with Vps4 and have provided leading mechanistic models for protein translocating AAA+ ATPases (Olivares et al., 2016).
evidence: This difference is noted with citations to the p97 and CDC48 structures.

claim: ClpX and HslU are not members of the classic clade but share notable similarities with Vps4 and have provided leading mechanistic models for protein translocating AAA+ ATPases.
source: Notable exceptions include p97 and CDC48, whose structures display rotational rather than helical symmetry (Banerjee et al., 2016; Xia et al., 2016), and ClpX and HslU, which are not members of the classic clade but share notable similarities with Vps4 and have provided leading mechanistic models for protein translocating AAA+ ATPases (Olivares et al., 2016).
evidence: This relationship is noted with a citation.

claim: Biochemical analyses of ClpX and HslU have argued for stochastic mechanisms by showing that just one active ATPase subunit per hexamer can drive translocation, albeit at much reduced efficiency.
source: In contrast to these sequential models, biochemical analyses of ClpX (Martin et al., 2005) and HslU (Baytshtok et al., 2017) have argued for stochastic mechanisms by showing that just one active ATPase subunit per hexamer can drive translocation, albeit at much reduced efficiency.
evidence: This alternative mechanism is described with citations to biochemical studies.

claim: A hexamer that has only one active ATPase site may allow inactive subunits to diffuse through the entire helical cycle, which could reconcile stochastic and sequential mechanisms.
source: A possible resolution is that a hexamer that has only one active ATPase site may allow inactive subunits to diffuse through the entire helical cycle.
evidence: This is a speculative proposal to reconcile different mechanistic models.

claim: A single active ATPase might drive the sequential conveyor-belt model, albeit rather poorly, like a 6-cylinder engine firing on just one cylinder.
source: Thus, like a 6-cylinder engine firing on just one cylinder, a single active ATPase might drive the sequential conveyor-belt model, albeit rather poorly.
evidence: This is a speculative analogy to explain how different mechanisms might be reconciled.

claim: The structure shows details of substrate interactions that are provided by a repeating array of dipeptide binding sites with the ESCRT-III peptide in a unique orientation.
source: In summary, the structure shows details of substrate interactions that are provided by a repeating array of dipeptide binding sites with the ESCRT-III peptide in a unique orientation.
evidence: This is a summary of the structural findings.

claim: The structure supports a sequential mechanism and explains the ability to translocate polypeptides with little sequence specificity.
source: It further supports a sequential mechanism and explains the ability to translocate polypeptides with little sequence specificity.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the mechanistic implications of the structure.

claim: Important future priorities include testing the generality of the structural observations and mechanistic implications.
source: Important future priorities include testing the generality of the structural observations, mechanistic implications, and the extent to which they may apply to other AAA+ ATPases.
evidence: This is a statement about future research directions.

claim: A total of 2,349 cryo-EM movies were recorded using a K2 Summit direct detector in counting mode with a pixel size of 1.10 Å.
source: A total of 2,349 cryo-EM movies were recorded using a K2 Summit direct detector (Gatan) in counting mode with a pixel size of 1.10 Å and at a dose rate of ~7.4 e-/pixel/sec.
evidence: This is a description of the data collection parameters.

claim: Each movie was recorded as a stack of 40 frames accumulated over 10 s, totaling ~62e-/Å2.
source: Each movie was recorded as a stack of 40 frames accumulated over 10 s, totaling ~62e-/Å2.
evidence: This is a description of the data collection parameters.

claim: 82,225 particles were used for the final round of RELION auto-refinement, producing a 3.2 Å resolution density map of Vps4.
source: 82,225 particles were sorted into a single class with high-resolution Vps4 features and used to generate the final 3.2 Å Vps4 reconstruction.
evidence: This is a description of the image processing and final reconstruction.

claim: B-factor sharpening of −125 Å2 was applied using an automated procedure in RELION postprocessing.
source: B-factor sharpening of −125 Å2 was applied using an automated procedure in RELION postprocessing (Rosenthal and Henderson, 2003).
evidence: This is a description of the map processing procedure.

claim: The refined model comprising the Vps4 ATPase domains of subunits A-E and ESCRT-III peptide has been deposited into the PDB with ID 6BMF.
source: The refined model comprising the Vps4 ATPase domains of subunits A-E and ESCRT-III peptide has been deposited into the PDB (RRID: SCR_012820; PDB ID: 6BMF).
evidence: This is a statement about data deposition.

claim: The complete model has been deposited into the PDB with ID 6AP1 together with the sharpened Hcp1-subtracted map at EMDB Accession Number EMD-8887.
source: The complete model, including regions not subjected to atomic refinement such as the 12 Vta1VSL domains and subunit F, has been deposited into the PDB (PDB ID: 6AP1) together with the sharpened Hcp1-subtracted map (RRID: SCR_003207, EMDB Accession Number EMD-8887).
evidence: This is a statement about data deposition.

claim: Two Vps4 subunits are expected to be disengaged from substrate through at least part of the reaction cycle.
source: Although our structure shows four intact dipeptide-binding sites and just one transitioning subunit, it is expected that two Vps4 subunits will be disengaged from substrate through at least part of the reaction cycle.
evidence: This is an inference about the reaction cycle based on the structural observations.

claim: Subunit E will disengage from substrate as it moves toward the F configuration while the F subunit is moving toward the substrate-binding A configuration.
source: This is because subunit E will disengage from substrate as it moves toward the F configuration while the F subunit is moving toward the substrate-binding A configuration.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the subunit transitions during the reaction cycle.

claim: The specific point in the reaction cycle captured in the structure corresponds to subunit E just starting to transition toward the F state.
source: The specific point in the reaction cycle captured in our structure corresponds to subunit E just starting to transition toward the F state, as indicated by the slight deviation of the DE interface from the configuration of AB, BC, and CD, and consistent with our structural interpretation that ADP is bound to subunit D (above).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the specific state captured in the structure.

claim: The stability of the captured state relative to other conformations along the reaction coordinate results from a combination of multiple factors, including the particular nucleotide (ADP·BeFx) and ESCRT-III peptide in the complex.
source: The stability of this state relative to other conformations along the reaction coordinate will result from a combination of multiple factors, including the particular nucleotide (ADP·BeFx) and ESCRT-III peptide in the complex.
evidence: This is an interpretation of factors affecting the conformational state.
